zh: 然而，鉴于我们先前对首要与次要能动性的讨论，有必要在某些方面对上述内容加以限定。抽象图案似乎显示母题之间的“因果”关系，而非母题之间的“施动者／受动者”关系，因为没有什么使我们认为图案中的母题本身是有感知的、有意图或欲望等。人体金字塔内部部分对整体的关系证明杂技演员方面的“首要”意图性——我们立即认出他们是意图性施动者——但我们印花帘布上的花卉母题之间的关系则不然，无论这些母题看起来多么活跃。这些母题只有“次要”能动性，它们显现能动性／意图性的效果，却不内在地拥有它。这些母题只彼此因果地互动，而非意图性地互动。然而，即便在这种情况下，我们确实在这里看到“意图性活动”，但它被移置到我们想象中的图案创作者身上，而非图案的物理构成成分上。复杂的因果关系，无论只是被“暗示”——如图案和抽象艺术中——还是被直接描绘——如贝尔尼尼的《普路托与珀耳塞福涅》中——所证明的复杂意图性能动性都不在索引本身，而在“幕后”，在艺术家巧妙的心智中。
en: However, in the light of our previous discussion of primary and secondary agency, it is necessary to qualify the above in certain respects. Abstract patterns appear to show ‘cause and effect' relations between motifs rather than ‘agent/patient' relations between motifs, in that nothing makes us think that the motifs in patterns are sentient in themselves, that they have intentions or desires etc. Whereas the part-to-whole relations within the human pyramid testify to ‘primary' intentionality on the part of acrobats whom we instantly recognize as intentional agents, the same is not true of the relations between the individual flower motifs on our floral drapes, be they ever so bustling. These motifs only have ‘secondary' agency, they manifest the effect of agency/intentionality without possessing it intrinsically. These motifs only interact causally with one another, not intentionally. However, even in this case, we do see ‘intentional activity' here, but it is displaced onto the imaginary creator of the pattern, rather than onto the physical constituents of the pattern. Complex causal relations, whether they are only ‘suggested'-as in patterns and abstract art-or whether they are depicted directly, as in Bernini's Pluto and Persephone, testify to complex intentional agency not in the index itself, but ‘off-stage', in the cunning mind of the artist.

zh: 3.11　艺术家-A → 艺术家-P
en: 3.11　Artist-A → Artist-P

zh: 在阐明了索引（或候选艺术品）相对于自身行使能动性的意义之后，让我转向艺术家所能行使的那种自反能动性。每位艺术家相对于他／她所行使的能动性都是受动者，事实上，艺术能动性不可能以其他方式进行。考虑画一件自己从未尝试画过的东西（比如一把奇彭代尔椅）的行为。人们想要制作一个指称这把椅子的索引。画的行为之前（无论被画对象是否在场）要先在脑中想象将要画成的图像。人们在内部预演必须画出的线条，然后画出它们（一幅画其实总是在画另一幅画，也就是脑中的那幅）。因为人的手实际上并不直接受自己想要画的心中所想或预期的线条的控制，而是受某种对内省完全不透明的神秘肌肉炼金术的控制，所以出现在纸上的线条总多少出乎自己的意料。在这一点上，人是自己绘画努力的观者；也就是说，人已成为受动者。在下意识层面，人问：“我会把这个（索引）认作我想画的那把椅子吗？”就好像它是别人画的一样。
en: Having explicated the sense in which an index, or candidate work of art, can exercise agency with respect to itself, let me turn to the kind of self-reciprocal agency which can be exercised by artists. Every artist is a patient with respect to the agency s/he exercises, indeed, artistic agency cannot proceed otherwise. Consider the act of drawing something that one has not attempted to draw before (a Chippendale chair, say). One desires to make an index which will refer to this chair. The act of drawing is preceded (whether the object to be drawn is present or not) by an act of visualization of the drawing to be made. One internally rehearses the line(s) which must be produced, and then draws them (a drawing is always really a drawing of a drawing, the drawing in one's head). Because one's hand is not actually directly controlled by the visualized or anticipated line that one wants to draw, but by some mysterious muscular alchemy which is utterly opaque to introspection, the line which appears on the paper is always something of a surprise. At this point one is a spectator of one's own efforts at drawing; that is, one has become a patient. Subliminally, one asks, ‘would I recognize this (index) as the chair I wanted to draw?' just as if it had been drawn by somebody else.

zh: 绘画以及大多数其他艺术技能（雕刻等）是所谓“弹道式”活动，即这类肌肉动作的速度快到对行动“结果”的认知加工只在行动完成之后、而非进行之中发生。（“弹道式”行为的原型是投掷。）最常见的是，如果一个人不太擅长绘画，他弹道式画椅子的动作的结果是令人沮丧的：“这把椅子不是我想画的那把——腿太长，而且整个歪歪扭扭”。无法“按意图”画出对象的准艺术家的受动者位置，是一种熟悉的困境。不过偶尔，由于肌肉碰巧一动，画出的线条实际上优于事先在脑中想象的那条。
en: Drawing, and most other artistic skills (carving, etc.) are what are known as 'ballistic' activities, muscular performances which take place at a rate such that cognitive processing of the 'outcome' of action only takes place after the act is complete, not while it is in progress. (The archetypal 'ballistic' behaviour is throwing.) Most often, if one is not very good at drawing, the result of one's ballistic chair-drawing gestures are frustrating: 'this chair is not the one I wished to draw-the legs are too long and it is all lop-sided'. The patient position of the would-be artist who cannot draw objects 'as intended' is a familiar predicament. Occasionally though, by a happy muscular fluke, the line drawn is actually superior to the one visualized beforehand.

zh: 这就是“生成—检验”序列，它是一切复杂认知活动的基本特征。丹尼特引用瓦莱里的话：“发明任何东西都需要两个人。一个想出各种组合；另一个作选择，从前者给他的众多东西中认出自己想要的、对自己重要的东西。我们所谓的天才，与其说是第一个人的功劳，不如说是第二个人能迅速看出摆在面前的事物有什么价值，从而加以取舍”（Dennett 1979: 71）。丹尼特用一章来为瓦莱里的论证辩护，尽管他不同意“选择者”必然比“生成者”更重要。瓦莱里显然正是在我们的意义上谈论 艺术家-A → 艺术家-P。当然，他谈的是诗，一种允许无限多次自我修正循环的艺术形式。这在图形／造型艺术中并非总是可能，因为“选择者”的擦除可能困难或不可能，而且如果任何给定“检验”循环的结果被认为不满意，整件作品可能就得重做。然而，人们确实在艺术家的准备性素描中看到大量“生成—检验”的证据，尤其是拉斐尔与米开朗基罗这类文艺复兴绘画艺术大师的作品，他们许多精妙绘出的形式从许多成团的试探性笔画中浮现出来，这些笔画被称为 abbozzi。
en: This is the ‘generate and test' sequence which is a fundamental feature of all complex cognitive performances. Dennett quotes Valery as saying ‘It takes two to invent anything. The one makes up the combinations; the other chooses, recognises what he wishes and what is important to him in the mass of things which the former has imparted to him. What we call genius is much less the work of the first one than the readiness of the second one to grasp the value of what has been laid before him and to choose it' (Dennett 1979: 71). Dennett devotes a chapter to vindicating Valery's argument, though he disagrees that ‘choosers' are necessarily more important than ‘generators'. Valery is obviously talking about Artist-A → Artist-P in precisely our sense. Of course, he is speaking of poetry, an art form which permits indefinitely many cycles of self-correction. This is not always possible in graphic/plastic art, where erasure by the ‘chooser' may be difficult or impossible, and the whole enterprise may have to be restarted if the results of any given ‘test' cycle are deemed unsatisfactory. However, one does see copious evidence of ‘generate and test' in artists' preparatory drawings, especially those by such Renaissance masters of the art of drawing as Raphael and Michelangelo, many of whose exquisitely drawn forms emerge out of clouds of provisional strokes known as abbozzi.

zh: 此外，常常有这样的情况，尤其是较复杂的素描、绘画或雕刻：艺术家会对最终成品感到意外，因为他事先在脑中预演的只是通往完成的一连串生成—检验循环，从来不是“最终成品”。达泽维多引用一位非洲雕刻者的证词，他说：
en: Moreover, it is often the case, especially with more complicated drawings, paintings, or carvings that the final product comes as a surprise to the artist simply because it never was the ‘final product' which was visualized beforehand, but only the successive generate-and-test cycles along the road to its completion. D'Azevedo cites the testimony of an African carver, who says:

zh: 我看见我做的东西［一个桑德面具］从妇女们的林地里走出来。它现在是一个昂然的男子 jina［灵］，有许多女人追着他。在这个世界上不可能看到比这更奇妙的东西。他的脸发着光，他东张西望，所有人都对这个美丽而可怕的东西感到惊奇。对我来说，它就像我做梦时看到的东西。我对自己说，这是我的 neme［亲熟之灵］带进我心智的东西。我说，我做了这个。一个人怎能做出这样的东西？我竟能做出这样令人敬畏的事。别人也要懂得其中的诀窍才能做到。没有女人能做。我觉得我生了孩子。（d'Azevedo in Forge 1973: 148）
en: I see the thing I have made [a Sande mask] coming out of the women's bush. It is now a proud man jina [spirit] with plenty of women running after him. It is not possible to see anything more wonderful in this world. His face is shining, he looks this way and that, and all the people wonder about this beautiful and terrible thing. To me, it is like what I see when I am dreaming. I say to myself, this is what my neme [familiar spirit] has brought into my mind. I say, I have made this. How can a man make such a thing? It is a fearful thing that I can do. No other man can do it unless he has the right knowledge. No woman can do it. I feel that I have borne children. (d'Azevedo in Forge 1973: 148)

zh: 艺术家在“受动者”反应——桑德面具在他心中激起的惊讶与敬畏（“一个人怎能做出这样的东西？”）——与自我赞许之间摇摆，后者源于这样一个事实：毕竟，产出它的是他的能动性——“我竟能做出这样令人敬畏的事。”不可能找到比这更明确的自反艺术能动性的实例了。雕刻者说在雕刻面具时他觉得自己“生了孩子”，以及他显然完全认同面具是一个活的、有知觉的、“东张西望”的存在，这也是非常有益的证词，支持了我们的一般假设：从人类学上说，艺术品最好被视为施动者的类型。我们偶像的制作者与我们其余人一样是热情的偶像崇拜者，因为在某种意义上，他们始终是自己亲手创造之物诞生时的被动观者。准确地说，这实际上是 [[艺术家-A] → 索引-A] ⟶ 艺术家-P。
en: The artist vacillates between the ‘patient' response, the astonishment and awe that the Sande mask produces in him—‘How can a man make such a thing?’—and self-approbation stemming from the fact that, after all, his was the agency which produced it-‘It is a fearful thing I can do.' It would be impossible to find a more explicit instance of self-reciprocal artistic agency than this. The carver's statement that in carving the mask, he thinks he has ‘borne children' and his evidently total commitment to the notion that the mask is a living, perceiving, being ‘looking this way and that' is also very helpful testimony bolstering our general hypothesis that, anthropologically speaking, works of art are best considered as types of agents. The makers of our idols are no less enthusiastic idolaters than the rest of us, because, in some sense, they always remain passive spectators at the birth of their very own creations. Correctly expressed, this is really [[Artist-A] → Index-A] ⟶ Artist-P.

zh: 最后，关于这一主题，我应当提示一个还要很久才会充分浮现的主题。艺术家不只产出单件的“作品”，他们有职业生涯，创作出自己的 œuvre（我用这个表示“作品”的法语词，用以指艺术家的“毕生作品”或“迄今全部作品”）。艺术家不只相对于他们此刻正在产出的“作品”是受动者。他们相对于自己曾产出的全部作品也可能处于受动者位置。例如，有些艺术家似乎不愿重复自己，或为要求他们不要重复的赞助人工作。例如，在我看来，普桑无论出于何种原因，很少复用彼此十分近似的构图，甚至可能从未复用过。如果普桑如我推测的那样遵循一条阻止他重复自己作品的原则，那么他的每一件作品都由所有其他作品否定性地规定，以便在构图上不像它们（当然他的个人风格保持相对一致）。另一方面，雷诺阿（人们可以通过参观费城的巴恩斯收藏来验证）画了大量彼此非常相似的“浴女”；他这样做，大概是因为他有一位赞助人（巴恩斯先生），这位赞助人最高兴的是他从雷诺阿那里购买的下一幅画与他先前从同一位艺术家那里购买的所有画相似。在两种情况下，艺术家相对于他在任何给定时间的全部 œuvre 都处于“受动者”位置，因为他当前的作品必须以某种特定方式与他先前的作品相关联。
en: Finally, on this subject, I should signal a theme which will not fully surface for a long while yet. Artists do not just produce singular ‘works', they have careers and produce an œuvre (I will reserve the French word for ‘work' to mean ‘lifetime work' or ‘all the work to date' of an artist). Artists are not just patients with respect to the ‘work' they are producing right now. They may also be in the patient position vis-à-vis all the work they have ever produced. Some artists, for instance, seem unwilling to repeat themselves, or work for patrons who demand that they should not do so. For instance, it seems to me that Poussin, for whatever reason, rarely if ever repeated a composition at all closely. If Poussin, as I hazard, observed a principle which discouraged him from repeating his own work, then his every work, individually, was negatively determined by all the others, so as not to resemble them in composition (though of course his personal style remained relatively consistent). Renoir, on the other hand (as one may verify by visiting the Barnes collection, in Philadelphia), painted a large number of ‘bathers' which resemble one another very closely indeed; and he did so, presumably, because he had (in Mr Barnes) a patron who was happiest if the next painting he purchased from Renoir resembled all the ones he had purchased from the same artist on previous occasions. In either case, the artist was in the ‘patient' position with respect to his total œuvre at any given time, to the extent that his current work had to be related, in a specific way, to his previous works.

zh: 3.12　接受者-A → 接受者-P
en: 3.12　Recipient-A → Recipient-P

zh: “接受者”这一范畴以一种非常显著的方式分裂为施动者与受动者，以至于人们可能想否认它真的是一个单一范畴。我所想到的区分，是“被动观者”（一般艺术公众）与“赞助人”之间的区分——后者实际委托艺术家生产艺术品，其作为赞助人的能动性因而被索引在他们促使其产生的艺术品中。从艺术人类学的观点看，赞助是一种非常重要的能动性形式。它似乎与单纯的观看大不相同，后者涉及相对于艺术品处于受动者位置、并被它“引发”反应（被打动、被迷住等）。另一方面，艺术赞助人也会被他们通过委托促使其产生的艺术品深深打动，或可能如此。委托上面引其话语的那位雕刻者的桑德会女成员（重要的、年长的女性），正是他描述为“追着”面具跑、受其灵性与阳刚魅力吸引的那些女性。这里，作为比较，是一位十四世纪观察者的引文，描述锡耶纳主教座堂杜乔《基督圣像》祭坛画的赞助人向该作品公开致敬：
en: The category of ‘recipients' splits into agents and patients in a very salient fashion, so much so that one might be tempted to deny that it was really a single category at all. The differentiation that I have in mind is that between ‘passive spectators' (the general art public) and ‘patrons'-those who actually commission artists to produce works of art, and whose agency, as patrons, is consequently indexed in the works of art they have caused to come into existence. Patronage is a very significant form of agency from the point of view of the anthropology of art. It seems very different from mere spectatorship, which involves being in the patient position vis-à-vis a work of art and being ‘caused' to respond by it (being impressed, fascinated, etc.). On the other hand, art patrons are profoundly impressed, or can be, by the works of art that they have caused to come into existence by commissioning them. The Sande adepts (important, senior, women) who commissioned the carver whose words are cited above, are the same women whom he describes as ‘running after' it, subject to its spiritual and masculine allure. Here, for comparison, is a quotation from a fourteenth-century observer, describing the public homage paid to Duccio's Majesty of Christ altarpiece for Siena cathedral by the patrons of the work:

zh: 在它［新画］被运往主教座堂的那天，店铺关门，主教率领一大群虔诚的教士与修士举行庄严游行，由九位执政官、公社全体官员和全体人民陪同，最尊贵者一个接一个手持点燃的蜡烛站在画旁，后面是妇女和儿童，怀着极大的虔诚。他们陪同该画前往主教座堂，按惯例绕坎波广场游行，所有钟欢乐地鸣响，出于对如此高贵的一幅画的崇敬。（约1311年手稿，引自 Holt vol. i 1957: 135）
en: And on the day that it [the new painting] was carried to the Duomo the shops were shut, and the Bishop conducted a great and devout company of priests and friars in solemn procession, accompanied by the nine signiors, and all the officers of the commune, and all the people, and one after another the worthiest with lighted candles in their hands took places near the picture, and behind came the women and children with great devotion. And they accompanied the said picture up to the Duomo, making the procession around the Campo, as is the custom, all the bells ringing joyously, out of reverence for so noble a picture as is this. (MS of c. 1311, cited in Holt vol. i 1957: 135)

zh: 委托该作品的主教与世俗当局（“九位执政官”），通过在公开场合显著地向他们自己能动性（经杜乔中介）的产物表示崇敬，来荣耀自己。当然，他们也在崇敬基督、圣母与诸圣，但真正被表示崇敬的对象其实是画本身，因为在当时，这类圣像被认为庇护供奉它们的公社的具体利益。杜乔的画将取代一幅更古老的圣像《大眼睛圣母》（已移至圣博尼法乔教堂），不久前锡耶纳军队在蒙特阿佩尔托战役中战胜佛罗伦萨人，就被归于这幅圣像。因此至关重要的是，新画应当“意识到”全镇都指望它“保佑我们免遭锡耶纳的叛徒与敌人之手”（同上）。
en: The bishop and lay authorities (the ‘nine signiors') who commissioned the work, glorified themselves by conspicuously showing reverence, in public, towards the product of their own agency (mediated by Duccio). They were, of course, also revering Christ, the Virgin, and the Saints, but it was really the picture itself which was the object towards which reverence was being shown, because, at that time, such holy icons were believed to protect the specific interests of the commune which harboured them. Duccio's picture was to replace an older icon, the Madonna of the Large Eyes (removed to the church of St Bonifacio), to which was attributed the victory of the Sienese forces over the Florentines at the recent battle of Monte Aperto. So it was most important that the new picture should ‘realize' that the whole town was depending on it to ‘keep us from the hands of traitors and enemies of Siena' (ibid.).

zh: 换言之，成功扮演“赞助人”角色的本质，恰恰要求对赞助的产物表示崇敬。赞助人是普通艺术公众中的同侪之首（Primus inter pares）。除非赞助人为自己所赞助的索引所打动，不论是公开表现出来、私下感到如此，或二者都有，否则赞助行为本身就是失败的，投入委托的资源就被浪费了。由此可知，赞助内在地有一个阶段，其中赞助人／施动者[接受者-A]是受动者[接受者-P]。
en: In other words, the very essence of successful performance of the ‘patron' role, necessitates a show of reverence towards the products of patronage. The patron is Primus inter pares among the general art public. Unless the patron is visibly and/or privately impressed by the index of which s/he is patron, the very act of patronage is a failure, and the resources which have been invested in the commission have been wasted. It follows that patronage has, intrinsically, a phase in which the patron/agent [Recipient-A] is a patient [Recipient-P].

zh: 3.13　原型-A → 原型-P
en: 3.13　Prototype-A → Prototype-P

zh: 索引再现原型，也因此承载原型的能动性。原型又可能成为这一索引的受动者。考虑来自一个老牌工业城镇的 H 议员（后任市长）的例子。H 议员的政党在该镇或多或少永久执政，而 H 是一位聪明能干的商人，通过委员会成员与主席的身份逐步晋升到议会领袖的位置，并成功地担任多年。城镇繁荣；在适当时候，他把领导权让给一位更年轻的同事，并接受市长职位。他庄严地主持公共活动，并在幕后为当地争取到众多丰厚的拨款和合同。他普遍受欢迎，甚至赢得昔日政敌的尊重。为纪念他的市长任期，议会一致提议他应坐下来让人画肖像，肖像将挂在议事厅一个荣耀的位置。他同意了，部分因为他知道妻子会多么高兴，部分因为他得到保证，不必忍受在艺术家画室里长时间坐着——作为一个仍然非常忙碌的人，他没时间。结果果然如此；艺术家只需一小时匆匆画若干速写，并从各种角度和距离拍大量照片。
en: The prototype of an index can be a patient with respect to the index which, by representing him or her, incorporates his or her agency. Consider the case of Councillor (later Mayor) H, hailing from an old-established industrial town. Councillor H's party is more or less permanently in power in the town, and H, who is an intelligent and efficient businessman, rises gradually through membership and chairmanship of committees to the position of leader of the Council, which he occupies successfully for a number of years. The town flourishes; at the appropriate time, he relinquishes the leadership to a younger colleague, and accepts the mayoralty. He presides with dignity over public functions, and, behind the scenes, helps to secure no end of lucrative grants and contracts for his community. He is universally popular, even winning the respect of his sometime political opponents. To commemorate his term as mayor, the Council unanimously propose that he should sit for his portrait, which will hang in the council chamber, in an honoured place. He agrees, partly because he knows how pleased his wife will be, and partly because he obtains an assurance that he will not have to endure long sittings in the artist's studio, which, as a still very busy man, he has no time for. And so it proves; the artist only needs an hour to dash off a number of quick sketches, and take a large number of photographs from various angles and distances.

zh: 指定的日子到了；议会集合，H 坐在市长宝座上，看着幕布拉开、他的形象显现。随着不可避免而冗长的致辞进行，H 有很好的机会细看自己的肖像。看着看着，他被恐慌与绝望袭击。因为在他看来，肖像不像一个人的再现，而像某种蔬菜，实际上是一个芜菁，带着令人反感的紫色光泽，长着些说不出名的赘生物，扭曲得难看。他不是虚荣的人；事实上多年来他每次照镜子都只是瞥上一眼，因为他甚至习惯在上班途中在轿车后座刮胡子，而不愿在浴室镜子前浪费宝贵时刻。但发现自己实际上多么丑陋，对他是一个可怕的打击，而他那离奇的芜菁脑袋与他所穿市长礼服的华丽之间的对比，使效果更糟。他不能因自己的狼狈而责怪肖像画家，因为他足够聪明，能领会肖像忠实于他的实际外貌；艺术家无论用相机还是画笔都不笨拙。但愿他笨拙才好！——但 H 出身学徒、浸染新教伦理，见到诚实的手艺就认得。“难道我就要这样被永远记住，”他纳闷，“作为一个芜菁？我的外貌到底有什么关系？为什么在与我有关的一切之中，偏偏我的脸必须被记住？”他希望自己能以无像的方式被纪念，用某种铭文牌匾之类的东西——但那得死了才行。最后，对于所发生的事，他除了自己、除了自己那张丑脸，无人可怪。如果他长得好看些，他的肖像就不会是这么可怕的东西。事实上，H 是他自己的受害者，他的实际外貌［原型-A］直接造成了肖像的这副模样，于是他自己遭殃［原型-P］。
en: The appointed day arrives; the Council is assembled, and, seated on the mayoral throne, H watches as the curtain is drawn apart and his image is revealed. As the inevitable, and prolonged, speeches proceed, H has a good opportunity to scrutinize his portrait. As he does so, he is assailed by panic and despair. For the portrait appears to him not to be a representation of a man, but of some vegetable, a turnip in fact, with a revolting purplish sheen to it, disfigured by nameless appendages. He is not a vain man; in fact it is years since he looked at himself for more than a moment at a time, for he is even accustomed to shave in the back of his limousine on the way to work, rather than waste precious moments before the bathroom mirror. But it is a terrible shock to him to discover how ugly he really is, and the effect is made worse by the contrast between his impossible turnip-head and the splendour of the mayoral costume he wears. He cannot blame the portraitist for his discomfiture, because he is intelligent enough to appreciate that the portrait is faithful to his actual appearance; the artist did not wield either his camera, or his brushes, inexpertly. Would that he had!-but H, who began life as an apprentice and imbibed the Protestant ethic, knows honest workmanship when he sees it. ‘Is this how I am going to be remembered forever,' he wonders, ‘as a turnip? What does my appearance matter anyway? Why does my face, of all the things to do with me, have to be remembered?' He wishes he could have been memorialized aniconically, by something in the nature of an inscribed plaque-but you have to be dead for that. In the end, there is nobody he can blame for what has happened but himself, his own ugly mug. If he were better-looking, his portrait would not have been such a horrid thing. As it is, H is his own victim, the victim of the direct causal influence his actual appearance [Prototype-A] has of the actual appearance of his portrait, which is so damaging to him [Prototype-P].

zh: 我承认，这是一个虚构的例子。但有许多真实的实例：肖像的模特儿感到自己是受害者。我可以引用有据可查的温斯顿·丘吉尔对格雷厄姆·萨瑟兰为他所作肖像的反感（他阻止了该画的公开流传）。这幅肖像被批评家广泛视为对这位伟大领袖的深刻研究，非常“逼真”。丘吉尔本人远远更喜欢卡什那幅英雄式的摄影肖像，他这样做也情有可原，尽管当代舆论认为卡什的照片远不如萨瑟兰的画真实。丘吉尔足够虚荣，在公开场合把形象的丑陋归咎于萨瑟兰而非自己，不像我们诚实的 H——H 知道在丑陋肖像的产生中能动性真正何在。但我认为他私下必定有过怀疑——否则他的反应不会如此激烈。
en: This, I admit, is an invented example. But there are numerous real instances of sitters for portraits feeling victimized. I might cite the well-documented antipathy felt by Winston Churchill towards the portrait made of him by Graham Sutherland (whose public circulation he prevented). This portrait is widely regarded by critics as a penetrating study of the great leader, very ‘true to life'. Churchill himself infinitely preferred the heroic photographic portrait by Karsh, as well he might have, in defiance of contemporary opinion which detects much less authenticity in Karsh's photograph than in Sutherland's painting. Churchill was vain enough to blame Sutherland, in public, for the ugliness of his image, rather than himself, unlike our honest H, who knows where agency really lies in the coming-into-being of ugly portraits. But I think he must have had private doubts-otherwise his reaction would not have been so violent.

zh: 索引的原型相对于自身行使的这类自反能动性／受动性，实际上对我们非常熟悉。如果我们照镜子，不喜欢所见、或确实赞许所见，我们就是作为受动者对一个我们自己是其施动者的索引（镜中像）作出反应。肖像画只是这一现象的一个特殊实例，由艺术家或摄影师的活动中介。只要原型确实是索引的成因，或者被认为是其成因，索引就至少可能反过来对原型造成影响，例如引起沮丧。那耳喀索斯的神话提供了一个非常纯粹的“无艺术家”的 原型-A → 原型-P 情形：他被自己在水池中的倒影（索引）迷住，导致他跌入水中溺亡。然而，大多数情况下索引对原型的效果并非主要由索引引起，而只是由索引中介，能动性在于艺术家或接受者。在丘吉尔／萨瑟兰的例子中，丘吉尔认为自己是艺术家能动性的受害者，而非自己作为一个丑陋之人之能动性的受害者。
en: This type of self-reciprocal agency/patiency exercised by the prototype of an index with regard to itself is actually very familiar to us. If we look into the mirror, and dislike what we see, or indeed approve of what we see, we are responding, as patients, to an index (the mirror image) of which we are the agents. Portraiture is only a special instance of this, mediated by the activities of an artist, or a photographer. Wherever there is really or supposedly a causal relationship such that the prototype is the cause of the index, it must be that the index is at least potentially able to cause effects (dismay, etc.) in the prototype. A very pure ‘artist-less' case of Prototype-A → Prototype-P is provided by the myth of Narcissus, whose beguilement by his own reflection (index) in a pool caused him to fall in, and drown. However, mostly the effects of the index on the prototype are not primarily caused by the index, but simply mediated by the index, and agency lies with the artist or the recipient. In the Churchill/Sutherland case, Churchill considered himself the victim of the agency of the artist, rather than his own agency as an ugly person.

zh: 盖尔在印本中引作 The Portrait of Dorian Grey，并称其为短篇小说。王尔德原作题为 The Picture of Dorian Gray。
en: Gell gives the title The Portrait of Dorian Grey and calls it a short story. Wilde’s work is titled The Picture of Dorian Gray.

zh: 关于“弹道式”活动，见下文 艺术家-A → 艺术家-P。
en: On ‘ballistic’ activity, see below on Artist-A → Artist-P.

zh: 另一方面，完全相同程度的能动性也可以归于成千上万涌向麦加、环绕并亲吻克尔白的朝圣者，他们同样是自愿的朝圣者，通过自己的努力寻求救赎，而非宗教自动机。文化所灌输的“观者具备能动性”这一信念在多大程度上成了一道遮幕，使现代人看不到自己的行动受到多少社会要求的驱使，这一点无法在此确定。就我们的目的而言，重要的是人们所持的信念，而非这些信念是否正当。
en: On the other hand, exactly the same degree of agency could be attributed to the thousands of pilgrims flocking to Mecca, to circumambulate and kiss the Kaaba, who are also voluntary pilgrims seeking salvation through their own efforts, not religious automata. The extent to which the culturally inculcated belief in agency of spectatorship is a screen, concealing from modern souls the extent to which their actions are driven by social imperatives, cannot be determined here. For our purposes what is important are the beliefs that people hold, not whether these beliefs are justified.
